newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs take hard skid, ignore Motta's denial.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs take hard skid, ignore Motta's denial.

text.p: Brazil shares ended 3.43 percent lower, ignoring comments by Communications Minister Sergio Motta denying his role in an alleged cash-for-votes scandal over a re-election bill, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 48 most traded stocks plummeted 365 points to 10,283 points.

Speaking at a news conference, Motta said a report published by Folha de Sao Paulo daily Wednesday that suggested he might be linked to a vote-buying scheme in which deputies allegedly received money to vote for the re-election bill was libelous and irresponsible.
"I reject and do not recognize any of the statements transcribed in the Folha de Sao Paulo newspaper," Motta told reporters.
Motta's denial, however, did not sway prices.
"His denials were not too convincing," a trader said.
"We have to wait and see how investigations into this scandal evolve," he added, noting that the market is likely to remain volatile awaiting further developments in the case.
Analysts also fear what Folha de Sao Paulo, which published reports on the alleged scam Tuesday and Wednesday, will bring in its Thursday's edition.

Benchmark Telebras preferred plunged 4.07 percent, closing at 129.70 reais, while its voting stock lost 3.9 percent to 123 reais. State oil firm Petrobras preferred closed off 2.59 percent at 226 reais.
Private CVRD preferred fell 1.24 percent, closing at 23.90 reais.
Federal power utility Eletrobras preferred plummeted 2.88 percent to 506 reais, leading the power sector index to fall 2.84 percent to 2,749 points.
Market turnover was heavy at 960.8 million reais ($906.4 million), one of the highest volumes of the year, the bolsa said.
